scope: Proposition 3.6 (Tightness) of the manuscript “Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders” (preprints/Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Quartic-Torus-Packets-for-Arbitrary-Orders-October-5-2026/quartic-torus-packets.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 015 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95c2a937da74097a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant C such that, for every fixed 0 < r < 1, lim sup X−→∞ µ∗{Λ : some 0 ̸= v ∈ Λ satisfies ∥v∥∞ < r} ≤ Cr4 . (3.22) The limit superior ranges over all primitive totally real quartic fields, all their orders, and all orderings of their real embeddings. Consequently, for every sequence of these packet measures µi = µOi,σi with Xi → ∞ and every ϵ > 0, there is a compact Kϵ ⊂ X4 with µi(Kϵ) ≥ 1 − ϵ for all sufficiently large i. Such a sequence is tight, and every weak subsequential limit is an A4-invariant probability on X4.
